metadata.author: Greg Paskal
metadata.description: Content Security Policy (CSP) header missing finding template with comprehensive guidance for all audiences including framework-specific implementation code, testing strategies, and infrastructure deployment procedures for XSS prevention.

EXECUTIVE.summary: Your website lacks Content Security Policy (CSP) headers, leaving it vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks that can steal customer data, inject malicious content, and damage brand reputation.
EXECUTIVE.businessRisk: High risk of data breach through XSS attacks. Attackers can steal customer credentials, payment information, and session tokens. Average XSS breach costs $4.24M (IBM 2023). Brand damage from defaced pages or injected malicious content. Customer trust erosion. Potential liability for compromised customer data.
EXECUTIVE.complianceImpact: OWASP Top 10 A03:2021 (Injection) non-compliance. PCI-DSS Requirement 6.5.7 violation (Cross-site scripting prevention). May trigger security audit findings and require immediate remediation for compliance certification.

PROJECT_MANAGER.summary: Missing Content Security Policy (CSP) headers expose application to XSS attacks. Need to implement CSP headers to meet security baseline requirements.
PROJECT_MANAGER.timeline: Should be addressed in current sprint. Implementation takes 2-4 hours plus testing. Critical for security certification and compliance audits. Medium priority unless active XSS vulnerabilities detected (then escalate to critical).
PROJECT_MANAGER.effort: 2-4 hours for initial CSP implementation. Additional 2-3 hours for testing and refinement based on content violations. Ongoing maintenance as application evolves.

DEVELOPER.summary: Content-Security-Policy HTTP response header is not present, allowing unrestricted JavaScript execution and inline scripts from any source.
DEVELOPER.technical: CSP is a W3C security standard that restricts resource loading and JavaScript execution to prevent XSS attacks. Without CSP, browsers will execute any JavaScript found on the page, including attacker-injected scripts via XSS vulnerabilities. CSP works as defense-in-depth - even if an XSS vulnerability exists, CSP can prevent the injected script from executing. Modern browsers (Chrome 25+, Firefox 23+, Safari 7+) fully support CSP Level 2. The policy is defined via the Content-Security-Policy header with directives like default-src, script-src, style-src, img-src, etc. Start with a restrictive policy and use report-only mode to identify violations before enforcement.
DEVELOPER.vulnerability: CWE-79 (Cross-site Scripting) - Without CSP, XSS attacks can: execute arbitrary JavaScript, steal authentication cookies/tokens, deface pages, redirect users to phishing sites, install keyloggers, exfiltrate sensitive data, perform actions as the authenticated user. CSP mitigates these risks by whitelisting allowed sources and blocking inline scripts.

SECURITY_ENGINEER.summary: Missing Content Security Policy enables unrestricted JavaScript execution, creating high-severity XSS attack surface across entire application.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.vulnerability: CWE-79 (Improper Neutralization of Input) and CWE-1021 (Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers). Absence of CSP eliminates critical defense-in-depth layer against XSS. Even with input sanitization, CSP provides additional protection against XSS exploitation. OWASP Top 10 A03:2021 Injection category.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.attackVector: Attacker exploits any XSS vulnerability (reflected, stored, DOM-based) to inject malicious JavaScript. Without CSP, browser executes injected code with full application privileges. Attack scenarios: session hijacking via document.cookie, credential theft through keylogging, Bitcoin mining scripts, cryptojacking, phishing overlays, ransomware deployment, botnet recruitment. XSS can bypass CORS, same-origin policy via exploited context.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.threatLevel: HIGH - XSS remains prevalent (detected in 40% of web applications, HackerOne 2023). CSP reduces XSS impact by 95% when properly implemented. Missing CSP increases dwell time for attackers post-XSS exploitation. Combined with other missing headers (X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options), creates compounding vulnerability.
SECURITY_ENGINEER.mitigationUrgency: Implement within current sprint (1-2 weeks). Start with report-only mode to identify violations, then enforce. Critical if active XSS vulnerabilities exist - escalate to immediate remediation. Deploy alongside input validation, output encoding, and secure coding practices.

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.summary: Web servers not configured to send Content-Security-Policy headers, requiring server-side configuration updates across all environments.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.technical: CSP headers must be added to HTTP responses at web server or application layer. Typically configured in Nginx, Apache, load balancers, or application middleware. Header syntax: Content-Security-Policy: policy-directives. Common starting policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'. Use Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only for testing without enforcement.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.scope: All web servers serving application traffic: production web servers, load balancers, CDN origin shields, API gateways, reverse proxies. Must be consistent across all environments (dev, staging, production). Affects all HTTP responses. Consider multiple domains/subdomains if using shared policy.
OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.monitoring: Set up CSP violation reporting endpoint. Monitor report-uri or report-to directive for policy violations. Track violation patterns to refine policy. Alert on unexpected violation spikes (may indicate XSS attempts). Use browser DevTools and CSP Evaluator for testing. Monitor for application breakage after CSP deployment.

QA_TESTER.summary: Missing CSP headers prevent security testing validation and block verification that application properly restricts resource loading and script execution.
QA_TESTER.testImplication: Cannot validate XSS prevention controls. Security testing tools (Burp Suite, OWASP ZAP) flag missing CSP as high-severity finding. Cannot verify defense-in-depth security posture. After CSP implementation, must test extensively for functionality breakage (blocked resources, inline scripts, eval() usage, third-party widgets).
QA_TESTER.riskIfNotFixed: Security audit failure. Penetration test findings. SOC 2 / PCI-DSS compliance gaps. Actual XSS exploitation in production. Customer data compromise. Regulatory penalties. Increased testing burden to manually verify XSS protection across all features.

# Django - Add CSP headers via django-csp middleware
# settings.py

# Install django-csp: pip install django-csp

INSTALLED_APPS = [
    # ... other apps
    'csp',
]

MIDDLEWARE = [
    # ... other middleware
    'csp.middleware.CSPMiddleware',
]

# CSP Configuration
CSP_DEFAULT_SRC = ("'self'",)
CSP_SCRIPT_SRC = ("'self'", "'nonce-{nonce}'")  # Nonce will be auto-generated
CSP_STYLE_SRC = ("'self'", "'unsafe-inline'")  # Consider using nonce for styles too
CSP_IMG_SRC = ("'self'", "data:", "https:")
CSP_FONT_SRC = ("'self'", "data:")
CSP_CONNECT_SRC = ("'self'",)
CSP_FRAME_ANCESTORS = ("'none'",)
CSP_BASE_URI = ("'self'",)
CSP_FORM_ACTION = ("'self'",)
CSP_OBJECT_SRC = ("'none'",)

# Use report-only mode for testing
# CSP_REPORT_ONLY = True

# CSP violation reporting endpoint
# CSP_REPORT_URI = '/csp-violation-report/'

# Alternative: Manual middleware if not using django-csp
# middleware.py
import secrets
import base64

class CspMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response
    
    def __call__(self, request):
        # Generate nonce
        nonce = base64.b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(16)).decode('utf-8')
        request.csp_nonce = nonce
        
        response = self.get_response(request)
        
        # Build CSP policy
        csp_policy = '; '.join([
            "default-src 'self'",
            f"script-src 'self' 'nonce-{nonce}'",
            "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'",
            "img-src 'self' data: https:",
            "font-src 'self' data:",
            "connect-src 'self'",
            "frame-ancestors 'none'",
            "base-uri 'self'",
            "form-action 'self'",
            "object-src 'none'",
        ])
        
        response['Content-Security-Policy'] = csp_policy
        
        return response

# In templates:
# {% load csp %}
# <script {% csp_nonce %}>
#   console.log('This script is allowed');
# </script>

# Or manually:
# <script nonce="{{ request.csp_nonce }}">
#   console.log('This script is allowed');
# </script>
django-python.testCode:
# pytest test for CSP header
import pytest
from django.test import Client
from django.urls import reverse

@pytest.fixture
def client():
    return Client()

@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_csp_header_present(client):
    """Test that CSP header is present in response"""
    response = client.get('/')
    
    assert 'Content-Security-Policy' in response.headers, \
        "Response should contain CSP header"

@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_csp_default_src_self(client):
    """Test that CSP includes default-src 'self'"""
    response = client.get('/')
    csp = response.headers.get('Content-Security-Policy', '')
    
    assert "default-src 'self'" in csp, \
        "CSP should include default-src 'self'"

@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_csp_no_unsafe_inline_scripts(client):
    """Test that CSP doesn't allow unsafe-inline for scripts"""
    response = client.get('/')
    csp = response.headers.get('Content-Security-Policy', '')
    
    # Extract script-src directive
    directives = csp.split(';')
    script_src = next((d for d in directives if 'script-src' in d), '')
    
    assert "'unsafe-inline'" not in script_src, \
        "CSP should not allow unsafe-inline for scripts"

@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_csp_includes_nonce(client):
    """Test that CSP includes nonce for scripts"""
    response = client.get('/')
    csp = response.headers.get('Content-Security-Policy', '')
    
    import re
    nonce_pattern = r"'nonce-[A-Za-z0-9+/=]+'"
    
    assert re.search(nonce_pattern, csp), \
        "CSP should include nonce for script-src"

@pytest.mark.django_db
def test_csp_blocks_object_src(client):
    """Test that CSP blocks object-src"""
    response = client.get('/')
    csp = response.headers.get('Content-Security-Policy', '')
    
    assert "object-src 'none'" in csp, \
        "CSP should block object-src"

generic.code:
# Generic CSP Implementation Guidelines

## Step 1: Choose Implementation Level

### Application Level (Recommended)
- Implemented in application code
- Allows dynamic nonce generation
- Framework-specific (see above)

### Web Server Level
- Nginx, Apache, IIS configuration
- Static policy (no nonces)
- Good for simple policies

## Step 2: Start with Report-Only Mode

Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only: default-src 'self'; 
  script-src 'self'; 
  report-uri /csp-violation-report

## Step 3: Build Your Policy

### Minimal Restrictive Policy:
Content-Security-Policy: 
  default-src 'self';
  script-src 'self';
  style-src 'self';
  img-src 'self' data:;
  font-src 'self';
  connect-src 'self';
  frame-ancestors 'none';
  base-uri 'self';
  form-action 'self';
  object-src 'none'

### With Nonces (Dynamic):
Content-Security-Policy: 
  default-src 'self';
  script-src 'self' 'nonce-{RANDOM_NONCE}';
  style-src 'self' 'nonce-{RANDOM_NONCE}';
  ...

### With Hashes (Static Inline Scripts):
Content-Security-Policy:
  script-src 'self' 'sha256-{HASH_OF_SCRIPT}'

## Step 4: Common Directives

- default-src: Fallback for unspecified directives
- script-src: JavaScript sources
- style-src: CSS sources
- img-src: Image sources
- font-src: Font sources
- connect-src: XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource
- frame-ancestors: Who can embed this page
- base-uri: Restricts <base> tag
- form-action: Where forms can submit
- object-src: <object>, <embed>, <applet> sources

## Step 5: Test and Refine

1. Deploy in report-only mode
2. Monitor violation reports
3. Identify legitimate violations
4. Adjust policy
5. Switch to enforcement mode
6. Continue monitoring

# Generic CSP Testing

## Browser DevTools Testing

1. Open browser DevTools (F12)
2. Go to Console tab
3. Navigate to your site
4. Look for CSP violation messages
5. Example: "Refused to execute inline script because it violates CSP"

## Command-Line Testing

# Check if CSP header is present
curl -I https://your-domain.com | grep -i content-security-policy

# View full CSP policy
curl -s -I https://your-domain.com | grep -i "^content-security-policy:"

# Test with verbose output
curl -v https://your-domain.com 2>&1 | grep -i content-security-policy

## Online Testing Tools

1. CSP Evaluator: https://csp-evaluator.withgoogle.com/
   - Paste your CSP policy
   - Get security analysis

2. Mozilla Observatory: https://observatory.mozilla.org/
   - Enter your domain
   - Get comprehensive security report

3. Security Headers: https://securityheaders.com/
   - Scan your site
   - View all security headers

## Automated Testing

# Using curl and grep
if curl -sI https://your-domain.com | grep -q "Content-Security-Policy"; then
  echo "✅ CSP header present"
else
  echo "❌ CSP header missing"
fi

# Using Python
import requests

response = requests.get('https://your-domain.com')
if 'Content-Security-Policy' in response.headers:
    print(f"✅ CSP: {response.headers['Content-Security-Policy']}")
else:
    print("❌ CSP header missing")
generic.dependencies: curl, browser with DevTools, optional: Python requests library

verificationSteps: Deploy CSP in report-only mode first: Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only
Set up violation reporting endpoint to collect CSP violations
Monitor violations for 24-48 hours in production-like environment
Analyze violation reports to identify legitimate resource loading
Refine CSP policy to allow legitimate sources while blocking unsafe practices
Test all application features: login, forms, AJAX, third-party widgets
Switch to enforcement mode: Content-Security-Policy (remove -Report-Only)
Monitor browser console for CSP violation errors
Test with CSP Evaluator (https://csp-evaluator.withgoogle.com/)
Verify no inline scripts without nonces, no 'unsafe-inline', no 'unsafe-eval'
Test across multiple browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
Run security scan (Observatory, SecurityHeaders.com) and verify CSP grade

apache.config:
# Apache - Add CSP header configuration
# /etc/apache2/sites-available/your-site.conf or .htaccess

<VirtualHost *:443>
    ServerName your-domain.com
    
    # Enable mod_headers if not already enabled
    # a2enmod headers
    
    # Basic CSP policy
    Header always set Content-Security-Policy "\
        default-src 'self'; \
        script-src 'self'; \
        style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; \
        img-src 'self' data: https:; \
        font-src 'self' data:; \
        connect-src 'self'; \
        frame-ancestors 'none'; \
        base-uri 'self'; \
        form-action 'self'; \
        object-src 'none'"
    
    # Report-Only mode for testing
    # Header always set Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only "..."
    
    # Other security headers
    Header always set X-Frame-Options "DENY"
    Header always set X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
    Header always set X-XSS-Protection "1; mode=block"
    Header always set Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    
    # Rest of your VirtualHost config
    DocumentRoot /var/www/html
    
    <Directory /var/www/html>
        Options -Indexes +FollowSymLinks
        AllowOverride All
        Require all granted
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>

# Alternative: .htaccess file
# <IfModule mod_headers.c>
#   Header always set Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; ..."
# </IfModule>

OPS_INFRASTRUCTURE.rollbackPlan:
1. Keep backup of current server configuration files
2. Document current header configuration (or lack thereof)
3. If CSP causes application breakage, temporarily switch to report-only mode
4. For Nginx: Comment out CSP header, run 'nginx -t', then 'nginx -s reload'
5. For Apache: Comment out CSP header, run 'apachectl configtest', then 'systemctl reload apache2'
6. For AWS ALB/CloudFront: Revert to previous configuration version
7. Analyze CSP violation reports to identify breaking resources
8. Refine policy to allow legitimate resources
9. Re-deploy updated policy in report-only mode
10. Test thoroughly before switching back to enforcement mode
